precepts.text: Philip found Nathanael: we have found him of whom Moses and the prophets did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.
precepts.point: Israel named sons the same name: Mattathias had Joannan and Jonathan, there were three Marys at the cross and Simons everywhere, so two Zerubbabels is no puzzle.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
In Matthew his own people asked, “Is not this the carpenter's son?” John shows his own disciples said the same thing: “Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

The son of who? The son of Joseph. The one Moses and the prophets wrote about is called by his disciple the son of Joseph, the carpenter.

And Matthew says he had brethren, James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and sisters, more than one: a bunch of siblings. James wrote the book of James and Judas wrote Jude. So you Christians who say Mary was a virgin who never had sex read this all the time. Now some hear us teach it and act like they came up with it, saying the Roman Catholic doctrine is wrong, playing catchup. Christ had a father and a mother, brothers and sisters.

precepts.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things were made by him, and without him was not any thing made that was made. The Father alone begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created. That is why he said to Philip, have I been so long with you and you have not known me? We have to shake the Christian thoughts, the Baptist and Catholic residue in the head.
precepts.point: Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end. It behooves us to learn God's laws, commandments, and statutes, because to set up a government you need everything we read at the beginning of class about what a community consists of. God's laws are going to filter everything for us. And we have to learn to think bigger: not a house, not property; the world is ours. In order for the world to be ours, we have to be able to set up all of those things.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
In case anyone is still confused about why Christ is called “The everlasting Father”, John 1 settles it. We have to shake the Christian thoughts.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God.” God is a plural there.

Then the part that matters: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ was not any thing made that was made. The Father only begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created.

That is why he said to Philip, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” I created all of this. That is too heavy for a Negro, because you have Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning too, but the Most High has shown us. Let it marinate.

So the child born and the son given in Isaiah 9:6, with the government upon his shoulder, is the same one who made all things: the Word, the mighty God, the everlasting Father.

precepts.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. Christ was the perfect, ultimate sacrifice.
precepts.point: Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. His people; that is who the sacrifice was for.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
We did not return to what the Most High commanded, the feasts he told us to go back to, and that is why we were in need of a saviour, an ultimate sacrifice. From Abraham to David, from David to the carrying away into Babylon, and from Babylon to Christ were fourteen generations each; we were always in slavery.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His name means he saves. His people: the Israelites only. From their sins. That is why he was the ultimate sacrifice.

His cousin John expounds on it: “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” The Lamb of God. Christ was that perfect, ultimate sacrifice, the lamb that takes away the sins of the people he came to save.

precepts.text: All things were made by him, and without him was not any thing made that was made. Christ was always the plan.
precepts.point: Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. His people; that is who the sacrifice was for.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ was always the plan. He is the author, the executive producer, whatever title you want to give him. From before the Old Testament, the body prepared for him in the volume of the book was the plan for saving his people from their sins.

John shows it: “All things were made by him”. All things were made by Christ: the principalities, the things you see out in space, the worlds, with an s. “And without him was not any thing made that was made.”

The one who made all things is the one who came as the Lamb of God to save his people. The sacrifices of the law, the seventh day and the rest it points to were all his from the beginning. So when the angel said “thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins”, it was the Maker of all things coming to fulfil the plan that was always his.

precepts.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: Christ pitched his tent among us.
precepts.point: The feast of tabernacles, seven days unto the Lord. Tabernacle, sukkot, booth: it means to dwell.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord.” Another word for tabernacles is sukkot, booths, and it means to dwell.

John shows who the feast points to: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,)”. The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us: he pitched his tent among us. Christ walked among us.

So the feast of tabernacles, like the sabbath, the passover, unleavened bread, firstfruits, trumpets and atonement before it, is a representation of Christ. The seven days of dwelling in booths look to the Son of God coming to dwell with his people in the flesh.

precepts.text: John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God. That male lamb of the first year represents Christ: he is that sacrifice. We do not sacrifice anymore, but we do have the dinner, with the understanding that the lamb represents Christ. Killing a lamb is not going to protect you from the wrath of God; believing in Christ and doing what is right is.
precepts.point: He took the cup, saying, Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. That blood that we used to put on the doorpost represents Christ's blood: it represents the new covenant, Christ coming and dying for our sins. So do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
At the Passover dinner Christ took the cup and said, “For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” The blood the Israelites put on the doorposts in ancient Egypt represented Christ's blood. It represented the new covenant: Christ coming and dying for our sins.

John shows who the lamb is: “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God”. Christ is called the Lamb of God. That male lamb of the first year represents Christ. He is that sacrifice.

So we do not sacrifice anymore, but we do have the dinner, with the understanding that the lamb represents Christ. Do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today; some brothers are crazy. Killing a lamb is not going to protect you from the wrath of God. Believing in Christ and doing what is right is what protects you from the wrath of God.

precepts.text: In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
precepts.point: 'Let there be light' is the first thing created, the light that is Christ, before the sun and moon existed.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
John opens the way Genesis does: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word that was with God is Christ. He was a God in the beginning, made in the image of his Father, creating angels, galaxies and planets. “The same was in the beginning with God”: two different persons, the Father and the Son.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” Then: “In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness.” That is the same light God brought out of his treasures in 2 Esdras 6, the light of Genesis 1.

John the Baptist “came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”, and “He was not that Light.” Christ is “the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world”: the true light God created on the first day.

precepts.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God: the us is the Father and the Son, and the image is the Father's and his Son's.
precepts.point: The whole class turns on who the us and the our are in that verse.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man: what Jacob saw, Nathanael is told he will see.
precepts.point: The Lord above it says, I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: The Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty and a terrible, which regardeth not persons.
precepts.point: Christ is a God and angels are gods, but he is not a god the way a man is a god; he is the God of gods, and the disrespect is unreal.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men: that is what the God of Israel did.
precepts.point: Christ is a God and angels are gods, but he is not a god the way a man is a god; he is the God of gods, and the disrespect is unreal.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: The Word was with God, and the Word was God; Christ is the almighty word that slew the firstborn in Egypt.
precepts.point: The destroyer was Christ, the almighty word of God. In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war into the midst of the land of destruction, and standing up filled all things with death. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury. Upon the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

precepts.why:
The destroyer that filled Egypt with death was the almighty word of God, and John says who the Word is: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word was with God, and the Word was God. That is Christ.

So the destroyer was Christ. The almighty word that leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war, that stood up and filled all things with death, is the same Word that was in the beginning with God. Christ slew the firstborn in Egypt, and where the Lord saw the blood on the lintel and the two side posts he passed over the door and would not suffer the destroyer to come in.

precepts.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; Christ was that lamb.
precepts.point: That is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: the law had a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice. Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ's coming.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
John bore the record: “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” Christ was that lamb, the Passover lamb without blemish, the flawless sacrifice the offerings of Leviticus were symbolic of.

Taking away the sin of the world goes back to presenting a glorious church without spot or wrinkle. The only way to be without blemish is through faith in Christ.

precepts.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; Christ is the atonement now.
precepts.point: Isaiah 53 cannot be speaking of David, who was already dead in Isaiah's day; it speaks of Jesus Christ, cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of the people, the ultimate sacrifice.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
The kid of the goats for a sin offering and the sin offering of atonement are laid aside in captivity, because the atonement is now Christ. “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.”

Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world: the lamb brought to the slaughter on whom the Lord laid the iniquity of us all. That is why we fast on the tenth day of the seventh month without the sacrifices.

precepts.text: In the beginning was the Word; this word was here before anything.
precepts.point: Many are my persecutors and mine enemies, yet do I not decline from Thy testimonies. Thy word is true from the beginning, and every one of Thy righteous judgments endureth for ever. This word was here before anything, before the Book of the Dead, before the Koran, all that other garbage.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” David says “Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.” This word was here before anything, before the Book of the Dead, before the Koran, all that other garbage.

That is why David loves the precepts and will not decline from the testimonies no matter how many his persecutors are: the word he holds to was here from the beginning, and its righteous judgments endure for ever.

precepts.text: Nathanael asks, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth, which shows how the place was regarded.
precepts.point: Nazareth had no reputation. That the messiah was raised there was itself a fulfilment of what the prophets spoke.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
When Herod was dead, Joseph brought the young child and his mother back into the land of Israel. But Archelaus reigned in Judea in the room of his father, so being warned of the Most High in a dream, Joseph turned aside into the parts of Galilee and dwelt in Nazareth, “that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.”

Nathanael shows how that place was regarded. When Philip tells him “We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph”, Nathanael answers, “Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?” Nazareth had no reputation; nobody expected anything good to come from there. Philip only says, “Come and see.”

That is the point of Matthew's words. The messiah was not raised in a city of renown, but in a place men looked down on, and that in itself was a fulfilment of what the prophets spoke.

precepts.text: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, was first a disciple of John, which is how water baptism carried on among some of the disciples.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
How did water baptism carry on among some of the disciples if Christ himself baptized not? “One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.” Andrew was first a disciple of John before he followed Christ.

Water baptism was what John did, and disciples who came from John carried it on. That does not make it the baptism Christ gives. His baptism, as John said, is with the Holy Ghost and with fire.

precepts.text: He was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.
precepts.point: The Word is Christ, and he was there in the beginning. The Word was with God, and the Word was of God: his wisdom and his power, which is why the same sentence can say both.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word is Christ, and he was there in the beginning. Revelation names him: “His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.”

The one clothed with a vesture dipped in blood is Christ, and his name is called The Word of God. So the Word that was with God in the beginning, “The same was in the beginning with God”, is Christ.

precepts.text: Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.
precepts.point: The Word is Christ, and he was there in the beginning. The Word was with God, and the Word was of God: his wisdom and his power, which is why the same sentence can say both.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
How can the same sentence say the Word was with God and the Word was God? “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.” Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.

The Word was with God, and the Word was of God: his wisdom and his power. That is why John can say both at once. The Word was with God in the beginning, and the Word was God's own wisdom and power.

precepts.text: By the word of the Lord were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.
precepts.point: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” The Word is Christ, and the psalm shows the word making everything: “By the word of the Lord were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.” The heavens and all the host of them were made by the word of the Lord, so nothing that was made was made without him.

precepts.text: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.
precepts.point: What gives life is the word itself. The flesh profits nothing; the words are spirit and they are life.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why: “In him was life; and the life was the light of men.” What gives life is the word itself. Christ says, “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” The flesh profits nothing; the words are spirit and they are life. The life that was in the Word is the life in the words he speaks.

precepts.text: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness.
precepts.point: What gives life is the word itself. The flesh profits nothing; the words are spirit and they are life.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why: “And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.” Christ says who that light is: “I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” The life that was the light of men is Christ, the light of the world. He that follows him does not walk in the darkness that comprehended it not, but has the light of life.

precepts.text: The blessing of all men and the covenant made to rest upon the head of Jacob, and his inheritance divided among the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: The blessing that came down on all men is traced in the scripture to one head, and rested on Jacob and was divided among the twelve tribes.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
John came “to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe.” He was not that Light; he prepared the way. That Light lights every man that comes into the world, and the blessing that came down on all men is traced in the scripture to one head: “With Isaac did he establish likewise for Abraham his father’s sake the blessing of all men, and the covenant, And made it rest upon the head of Jacob.”

“He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.” The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob, and his inheritance was divided among the twelve tribes.

precepts.text: Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.
precepts.point: His own are named all through the scriptures: the people the law was appointed to, and sin is the breaking of that law.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why: “He came unto his own, and his own received him not.” His own are named all through the scriptures: the people the law was appointed to. And sin is the breaking of that law: “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” Sin is the transgression of the law, the law appointed to his own.

precepts.text: He established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel.
precepts.point: His own are named all through the scriptures: the people the law was appointed to, and sin is the breaking of that law.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why: Who are his own? “For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children”. The law was appointed in Israel, so his own are Israel, named all through the scriptures. He came unto his own, the people the law was appointed to, and his own received him not.

precepts.text: Beloved, now are we the sons of God: and when he shall appear, we shall be like him.
precepts.point: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
John writes it plainly in his epistle: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”. That is the power spoken of in John 1:12, the power given to as many as received him and believe on his name: to become the sons of God.

“therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” The world did not know Christ, and so it does not know his sons either.

“Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.” Now, already, we are the sons of God; and when he appears, we shall be like him. That is what it is to be born “not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.”

precepts.text: He hath given the way of knowledge unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. That names who the beloved are.
precepts.point: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
Baruch says, “This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him”. Then he names the ones God gave his knowledge to: “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

That names who the beloved are. When John writes “Beloved, now are we the sons of God”, the beloved are Jacob his servant, Israel his beloved. The way of knowledge was given to Israel, and it is those who received him, who believe on his name, that are given power to become the sons of God.

precepts.text: He gave his only begotten Son. A father and a son are two, which is what the verse says on its face.
precepts.point: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” The Word was made flesh, and we beheld his glory, “the glory as of the only begotten of the Father”; here Christ says whose only begotten Son that is. God gave his Son.

A father and a son are two, which is what the verse says on its face. The Father gave; the Son was given. The Word made flesh that dwelt among us, full of grace and truth, is the only begotten Son of the Father, not the Father himself.

precepts.text: They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth, for grace and mercy is to his saints.
precepts.point: Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
“For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.” Solomon shows where grace and truth are found and who they are for: “They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth: and such as be faithful in love shall abide with him: for grace and mercy is to his saints, and he hath care for his elect.”

Grace and mercy are said in the scriptures to be with his saints. They that put their trust in him understand the truth, and he has care for his elect. The grace and truth that came by Jesus Christ belong to his saints, his elect, the ones faithful in love that abide with him.

precepts.text: His grace and mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect unto his chosen.
precepts.point: Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
Solomon says it a second time: “This the people saw, and understood it not, neither laid they up this in their minds, That his grace and mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect unto his chosen.”

His grace and mercy is with his saints, and he has respect unto his chosen. The people saw it and understood it not, and did not lay it up in their minds. So when John says “grace and truth came by Jesus Christ”, that grace is with the saints, his chosen, the ones he has respect unto.

precepts.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.
precepts.point: Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
David tells what the truth is: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is named in the psalm as the law itself.

So “grace and truth came by Jesus Christ” does not put the law away. Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator. The law is the truth, and the truth came by Jesus Christ with grace, through that mediator, instead of a man's own blood.

precepts.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; that he should be made manifest to Israel.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son”. This follows straight on from the serpent lifted up in the wilderness for Israel, and it is the same people in view. John's own gospel names who the world is.

John the Baptist said, “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” Then he said why he came: “And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water.” The Lamb that takes away the sin of the world was to be made manifest to Israel. The world whose sin he takes away is the one he was made manifest to: Israel.

precepts.text: Christians misuse "he came unto his own, and his own received him not," but the same passage says as many as received him were given power to become the sons of God.
precepts.point: This five thousand disproves the Christian claim that the Jews all rejected Christ. He came unto his own, meaning the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation, and only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed and were zealous of the law.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Christians misuse “He came unto his own, and his own received him not” to say the Jews all rejected Christ. But the same passage says, “But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name”.

His own were the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation. Only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed, five thousand men here.

Many still hear and believe today, and it is mainly black men leaving the dead churches, because the church gives them no purpose, no structure, no discipline and no position to lead, teaching them to be docile and subservient.

precepts.text: When John stood with two of his disciples and said, Behold the Lamb of God, the two heard him and followed Jesus; John's disciples went and followed Christ.
precepts.point: This seems to contradict everything taught earlier about Christ's baptism not being water. Philip baptized the eunuch in water because, like Ezra and others, some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism; John understood his own place and told his disciples to follow Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“Again the next day after John stood, and two of his disciples; And looking upon Jesus as he walked, he saith, Behold the Lamb of God! And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.” John's disciples went and followed Christ.

This is why Philip baptizing the eunuch in water seems to contradict everything about Christ's baptism not being water. Like Ezra and others, some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism. John himself sent his disciples on to Christ, and they brought John's water baptism with them.

precepts.point: This verse also shows that Christ and God are two separate entities: 'Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,' showing they are two separate entities. God is the Father and Christ is the Son of God.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
The grace Paul speaks of is grace and mercy given by Christ. Prior to Christ, under the old covenant, there was no mercy given. “For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.”

That does not mean the law was done away with. The law was also given by Jesus Christ; the only difference is that mercy was given through the blood of Christ. Grace and truth came by him.

The verse also shows that Christ and God are two separate entities: “Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ.” God is the Father and Christ is the Son of God.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 6 The 4 Horsemen

precepts.why: I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seals: this is the precept for the Lamb, because people get dumb as hell; Christians make me sick, these damn Christian commentaries are dumb as hell. What is the Lamb? “And looking upon Jesus as he walked, he saith, Behold the Lamb of God!” That is what we wanted. So in Revelation 6:1 the Lamb is talking about Christ.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why: “He that cometh after me is preferred before me: for he was before me.” John the Baptist is speaking more deeply than the order in which they appeared on earth. Christ was the first of the Father's creations and his delight, as Proverbs 8 explains. His preference and existence precede John.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why: “Then I was by him, as one brought up with him”. That is the meaning of the Word being with God. Christ was with the Father before everything else was made, not merely a prophet introduced after the world already existed.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why: Son of man, because he came from man. People play games: son of man because he didn't have no father. You simple as hell. Son of man because he had a father. “Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.” Son of man: Jesus, the son of Joseph.
